events.title: The Battle of the Standard
events.shortBlurb: Under a mast bearing a crucifix and the banners of the northern saints, the levies of Archbishop Thurstan broke the invasion of David of Scotland…
body: In the anarchy of King Stephen's reign, David I of Scotland came down into England for the third time in 1138, professing the cause of his niece the Empress Matilda, and wasting the country south over the Tyne and the Tees toward York. Thurstan, the aged Archbishop of York, gathered the levies of the north to meet him.

The armies met on Cowton Moor, two miles north of Northallerton, on 22 August 1138. In the midst of the English host stood a cart, and on it a ship's mast, from which hung a silver crucifix and the banners of St. Peter of York, St. John of Beverley, and St. Wilfrid of Ripon — the standard that gave the battle its name. Thurstan, too old and sick to ride with them, sent Ralph, Bishop of the Orkneys, in his place, who absolved the host in the archbishop's name and promised the kingdom of heaven to those who should fall.

The wild charge of the Galwegians broke upon the dismounted knights and the arrows of the Yorkshire bowmen; the Scots were routed with heavy loss, and David barely brought his remnant back to Carlisle. By Michaelmas a truce was made at Roxburgh, and the north had peace.

sources.text: Richard of Hexham, De gestis regis Stephani (c. 1140), ed. R. Howlett, Rolls Series (1886)

events.title: The death of St. Philip Benizi
events.shortBlurb: The Servite general who had hidden in a cave rather than be made pope, and spent his office making peace between the factions of Italy, died at Todi…
body: Philip Benizi was born at Florence on 15 August 1233, studied medicine at Paris and Padua, and after a year's practice laid aside the physician's art for the new order of the Servants of Mary at Monte Senario. Ordained priest, he rose to be prior general in 1267, and governed the Servites for the rest of his life.

When Clement IV died in 1268 and Cardinal Ottobuoni named Philip in the conclave at Viterbo as a candidate for the papacy, he fled to a cave on Monte Senario and hid until Gregory X was chosen. He sat at the Second Council of Lyons in 1274, and in the faction-ridden cities of Italy he went about as a maker of peace; at Forlí, struck in the face by a young hothead named Peregrine Laziosi, he won him to penance and to the order, and to a saint's life.

At the chapter of 1285 his brethren, refusing his resignation, chose him general once more. Travelling, he came to Todi, and there, on the octave of the Assumption, 22 August 1285, he died. He was the first Servite to be canonized, raised to the altars by Clement X on 12 April 1671; his feast is kept on 23 August.

sources.text: Catholic Encyclopedia (1913), “Servants of Mary (Order of Servites)”
Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 23 August
